contexts.text: In . etc., each and all things are representative of the falsification of truth, and of punishment on that account, even to this, that they were destroyed by such things as are signified by to lap waters with the tongue, like a dog ().
The flame lapped round about the hand.
The great head (of the turtle) licked their hands.
The black cow licked her hand.
The little dog... licked her lips.
By enemies are signified evils, of which it is said that they shall lick the dust (), that is, that they are damned.

Py Midian are here () meant those who do not care for truth, because they are merely natural and external; and therefore they were smitten by those who lapped waters in their hand with their tongue, as a dog lappeth; for by these are meant those who have an appetite for truths, thus who from some natural affection strive to know truths; for by a dog is signified appetite and desire; by waters, truths; and by to lap them with the tongue, is signified to have an appetite for, and to strive after from desire.
The eagles licked up the viscosity like water.
